description:
The full record for one place you already know by id: every dog rule with its display text, the rules list, and each source with its URL, publisher, capture date and quote. A place on I-5 in California also carries its axis position (s meters from San Ysidro on the I-5 centerline, Caltrans mile, meters off the road, side of northbound travel, road elevation, strip) and, when it is the dog side of a paired stop, that pair: the exit and the people-stops near it (counted from OpenStreetMap, never named, not verified for restrooms).

Takes a place id, as returned in every search result; a place's exact name works too, and a near miss resolves to the one clear match (labeled resolved_from). An id nothing matches comes back as an answer with close matches (did_you_mean), not an error. Example: id="carmel-beach".

response_format.description: 'markdown' for readable text, 'json' for structured data

name: dogpolicies_get_place

axis.description: Where the place sits on the I-5 axis: s meters from San Ysidro, Caltrans mile, meters off the road, side of northbound travel, road elevation, strip; null off I-5

citation.description: Copy-ready citation: answer, source, date checked, record URL, license

code.description: With an outcome other than ok: not_found, invalid, unavailable

confidence.description: stated: the place's own source says it; inferred_from_agency: an agency-wide rule; inherited_brand: the chain's policy, not confirmed by this hotel

did_you_mean.description: Close matches to what was asked for: towns, places, slugs or brands, best first

anyOf.description: fresh: inside its review interval; due: past it; stale: past twice it, confirm before you go; unreadable: the last check could not read the source

nearest.description: When nothing is inside the radius: the nearest places in the data, with distance_miles

next.description: Calls that would answer the question, in words

not_stated.description: Expected facts the sources do not state; never guess these

outcome.description: Absent or ok: a normal answer. no_match: nothing in the data matches, see did_you_mean, nearest and next. bad_input: the arguments cannot be used as given, see next. partial: some of the ids were found, see missing. unavailable: a live source could not be read. None of these is an error.

resolved_from.description: Set when the id or name given was not exact and this record was the one clear match

confidence.description: stated: the place's own source says it; inferred_from_agency: an agency-wide rule; inherited_brand: the chain's policy, not confirmed by this hotel

freshness.description: fresh: inside its review interval; due: past it; stale: past twice it, confirm before you go; unreadable: the last check could not read the source

uid.description: Stable id that survives a rename

title: Get place details
